subject: Safety holdback and fallback rates for Hosted API - minimum spend & on-demand over-commit
messages:
From: Anna Rivera <anna@tidelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - minimum spend / on-demand fallback question

Hi Vanessa,

Quick note from Tidewater: we're evaluating Redwood for a public-facing feature that will see very spiky traffic (daily peaks with a few multi-hour surges). We want to understand how Hosted API pricing would work if we commit to a baseline but regularly need large on-demand bursts. Two specific questions: 

1) Minimum spend - what's the smallest monthly commit you can reasonably support for a pilot (we're thinking ~$10k/month)? Any minimums, billing cadence, or true-up mechanics to be aware of?

2) Overage / on-demand fallback - if we exceed commit, what rate applies for on-demand tokens? Do you offer tiered burst pricing or an emergency cap for short surges? We need to show procurement an example with numbers for a 72-hour spike (approx +600% above baseline).

I've attached a rough projection of our traffic pattern and token estimates. We're not ready to sign an enterprise commit, but procurement will want clarity on worst-case cost.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Rivera
Head of Platform
Tidewater Labs
Attachment: current_usage_projection.csv (CSV, 24 KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Rivera <anna@tidelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - minimum spend / on-demand fallback question

Hi Anna — thanks for the projection, this is exactly the sort of spike we see with gaming and retail workloads. High level first, then a concrete example you can share with procurement.

High-level options we typically offer for pilot/POCs:
- Soft pilot commit (recommended): minimum monthly commit in the $8k–$15k range depending on term; includes guaranteed reserved capacity and a 30% burst allowance at commit rates.
- On-demand fallback (no commit): on-demand per-token rate at list price with no reserved capacity; suitable for short-lived tests but not cost-predictable for sustained bursts.

On overage / burst mechanics (what you asked):
- Overage (on-demand over commit): 1.6x the committed per-token rate by default. This is applied to tokens consumed beyond the monthly commit.
- Burst tiers: if a customer runs sustained bursts above 2x baseline for more than 24 hours, we step down into a burst-tier pricing ladder: 1.4x for sustained bursts up to 2x baseline, 1.2x for long-tail (multi-week) steady increases — tiers are negotiable per-account.
- Emergency grace cap: for unexpected short spikes (<=72 hours) we can offer a one-time emergency grace rate of 1.25x list for the first 72 hours if you commit to a 12-month term within 30 days of the spike.

Concrete example (using numbers from your CSV):
- Baseline commit: $12,000/month -> covers ~4M tokens at committed rate ($0.003/token equivalent).
- 72-hour spike adds ~2.4M tokens (~+600% on a single day peak).
- Tokens beyond commit (~2.4M) billed at 1.6x committed rate -> incremental cost ~ $0.0048/token -> ~ $11.5k for the overage.
- If we agree to the emergency grace cap (1.25x) and a 12-month term, that overage would be ~$7.5k instead.

Attachments: I attached a short two-page breakdown of the scenarios (proposed_pricing_breakdown.pdf) so procurement can see line items.

Next steps: happy to schedule a 30-min call with procurement and your billing lead to run through exact numbers and term options. If you want, I can include a sample contract clause for the emergency grace and a simple playbook for burst detection/fallback.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, East Coast
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_pricing_breakdown.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety holdback - negotiation notes

Vanessa — quick internal note/suggested concession before we take to procurement:
- If Tidewater signs a 12-month commit at $12k/mo (we get predictable revenue), offer a 10% discounted burst rate for the first 3 months (so emergency grace moves from 1.25x to effectively ~1.125x on their overage during that window). That gives them runway to launch without a big surprise bill and gives us time to monitor usage patterns.
- Keep the default overage at 1.6x after the initial window; allow a clause to revisit after month 3 with telemetry thresholds.
- Approve waiving the setup fee for pilots < 6 months to remove procurement friction.

I'll be on the call if you want me to surface this concession.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
